The '''2026 WAFL season''' was the 142nd season of the [[West Australian Football League]] (WAFL), the highest-level men's [[Australian rules football]] competition in [[Western Australia]]. The season began on 3 April and concluded on 20 September.<ref name=one>{{cite web|url=https://wafootball.com.au/news/easter-launch-for-2026-sullivan-logistics-wafl-season/|title=Easter launch for 2026 Sullivan Logistics WAFL season|work=WA Football|date=20 December 2025|author=Mark Readings}}</ref>

{{WAFL|PT}} won the [[List of WAFL premiers|premiership]] for the fourth time, defeating {{WAFL|Cla}} by 62 points in the [[2026 WAFL season#Grand Final|Grand Final]]. It marked Peel's second title in three seasons and made the club the most successful side through the last 10 years, having won all four of their premierships in that time. 

==Background==
[[South Fremantle Football Club|South Fremantle]] entered the season off the back of their 15th premiership, having defeated [[East Perth Football Club|East Perth]] by two points in the [[2025 WAFL season#Grand final|grand final]]. WA Football confirmed that several of the rule changes adopted for the [[2026 AFL season]] would also be incorporated in the WAFL, including the discontinuation of the centre bounce and a last disposal out of bounds rule between the 50-metre arcs, among others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wafl.com.au/article/26620|work=WA Football|date=27 November 2025|title=WAFL joins AFL with rule changes for 2026}}</ref>

==Representative match==
===WAFL vs SANFL===
For the eighth successive season, an interstate representative match was fixtured between the WAFL and [[South Australian National Football League]] (SANFL), with the two teams playing for the [[Haydn Bunton Jr.|Haydn Bunton Junior]] Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sanfl.com.au/league/news/2026-hostplus-sanfl-league-fixture-release/|title=2026 Hostplus SANFL League Fixture Released|date=24 December 2025|work=sanfl.com.au|quote=The West End State team will have its sights set on regaining the Haydn Bunton Junior Cup in the KIA State Game against the WAFL on the weekend of Saturday May 16 after it hosts the VFL at Stratarama Stadium on Saturday April 11 as part of the AFL Gather Round festivities.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://wafootball.com.au/news/historic-kia-state-game-triple-header-locked-in/?_gl=1*1hp34kn*_gcl_au*MTEyMzgwMDg5OC4xNzc1NjQ4NDY4|title=Historic Kia State Game triple-header locked in|work=WA Football|date=17 April 2026|author=Jordan McArdle}}</ref>
